outputs.exact_statement: For every datum [eq:gauge-data], every commuting flavor torus $F$, and every regular stability character $\nu$, both coefficient maps are surjective and have the same kernel. They therefore induce a canonical isomorphism of graded $R$-algebras $$H_F^*(X;\mathbb C)\ \cong\ \mathbb C[Y_{\mathfrak f}^{\nu}].$$ The gradings are ordinary cohomological degree and BFN homological degree, respectively. The assertion includes the empty case, whose ring is zero.

For the purposes of Theorem 1, one may assume that the flavor action assigns a character to each arrow summand and acts diagonally on each framing multiplicity space. Adding or removing a $G$-trivial representation with any flavor action preserves both coefficient-algebra quotients and all stability conditions.

Let $F\to F'$ be a homomorphism of algebraic tori, and suppose the action on $N$ is obtained by restriction of an $F'$-action commuting with $G$. Then the natural maps are isomorphisms $$\begin{aligned}
 A_{F'}\otimes_{H_{F'}^*(\mathrm{pt})}H_F^*(\mathrm{pt})&\ \cong A_F,\\
 B_{F'}\otimes_{H_{F'}^*(\mathrm{pt})}H_F^*(\mathrm{pt})&\ \cong B_F.
\end{aligned}$$ They respect the coefficient maps, both gradings, and convolution.

Let $\theta$ be a rational character parameter for which every semistable point of $\mu^{-1}(0)$ is stable and has trivial stabilizer. There is a neighborhood $U$ of $\theta$ in $X^*(G)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb R$ such that the stable and semistable loci are unchanged for every rational $\theta'\in U$. One may choose such a $\theta'$ outside all proper hyperplanes $\theta'\cdot\mathbf b=0$ with $0<\mathbf b\leq\mathbf v$, and then clear its denominators by a positive integer. Empty loci are included.
For every datum and regular stability in Theorem 1, the coefficient map induces a graded $R$-algebra surjection $$\label{eq:stable-pair-surjection} B_F\twoheadrightarrow H_F^*(X).$$

Let $\mathcal P$ be a principal $G$-bundle on $\mathbb P^1$, equipped with a frame at infinity, and let $\sigma$ be a global section of $\mathcal P\times_G(T^*N)$. Suppose that its value $\sigma_\infty$ in this frame is $\nu$-stable and has trivial stabilizer. Then $\deg\mathcal L_\nu\geq0$. If $\deg\mathcal L_\nu=0$, the pair $(\mathcal P,\sigma)$ has a unique trivialization, agreeing with the given frame at infinity, in which $\sigma$ is the constant section $\sigma_\infty$.*


*In particular, suppose that $\mathcal P$ is specified by a lattice $b\in\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}_G$, with its usual trivialization on $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0\}$. In the degree-zero case its topological class is zero and $$\label{eq:based-loop-trivialization}
 b=hG(\mathcal O),\qquad
 h\in G(\mathbb C[t^{-1}]),\qquad h(\infty)=1.$$ In the off-zero frame, the section is $h\sigma_\infty$.

The support of $\Phi_{W_B}\mathbb C_{M_B}$ is contained in the closed locus $\Sigma_B$ defined by $$\label{eq:stable-critical-equations} n\in s+L_-, \qquad p+y\in gN^*(\mathcal O)/t^lN^*(\mathcal O), \qquad b=gG(\mathcal O).$$ Here $n\in E_b$ is already part of the definition of $M_B$. If $B$ lies in a nonzero topological component whose character-line degree is nonpositive, then $\Sigma_B$ is empty and the test in [eq:stable-test-proper] is zero.

Under the abelianization embedding of Proposition 3, the no-flavor Coulomb algebra is $$\label{eq:laurent-model} A_0=\left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\mathbb Z^\Omega}P r_\lambda\right)^{\mathcal W}.$$ The identification preserves the coefficient ring $R_0=P^{\mathcal W}$ and the topological grading.
For every finite array $m$, the algebra $P_m/J_m$ is finite dimensional. Consequently $h_m(q)$ is a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients.

Suppose that the quiver has a loop at every vertex of positive dimension. At determinant stability, the coefficient map induces a canonical isomorphism of graded $R_0$-algebras $$B_0\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^*(X_{\det}(v,w);\mathbb C).$$

Fix a quiver and dimension and framing vectors. The ordinary Betti numbers of $X_\theta=\mu^{-1}(0)/\!/_{\theta}G$ are independent of the regular character $\theta$, where regular means that every semistable point is stable and the action on the semistable locus is free. Empty quotients are included.

For a fixed regular stability, suppose that the coefficient map induces $B_0\simeq H^*(X)$. Then, for every commuting flavor torus $F$, the map of Proposition 8 is an isomorphism $$B_F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H_F^*(X)$$ of graded $R$-algebras.

For every finite quiver and every dimension and framing vector, at the determinant stability used in Corollary 20, the coefficient map induces an isomorphism of graded $R_0$-algebras $$B_0\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^*(X).$$
For every datum in the statement of Theorem 1, the coefficient map induces a canonical isomorphism of graded $R$-algebras $$B_F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H_F^*(X).$$

For every unframed quiver $\Gamma$ and dimension vector $\mathbf d$, the two halves above admit $S$-linear algebra maps to an algebra of difference operators defined without inverting rotation or arrow parameters. They send $e_{\mathbf n,g}$ and $f_{\mathbf n,g}$, for $\mathbf n\leq\mathbf d$, to nonzero constant multiples of the positive and negative fundamental operators, respectively; they send these elements to zero when $\mathbf n\not\leq\mathbf d$. After setting $\hbar=0$, $w_{ia}=x_{ia}$, and $u_a=-f_a$, where $f_a$ is the prescribed flavor weight of arrow $a$, their images lie in $A_{\Gamma,\mathbf d,F}$. Dimension-vector degree becomes positive, respectively negative, topological charge. These maps preserve finite polynomial-coefficient identities under this specialization.

Let $\Gamma$ be an unframed quiver with dimension vector $\mathbf d$, and let a flavor torus act by a character on each arrow. Write $A_{\Gamma,\mathbf d,F}$ for its commutative Coulomb algebra and $R_{\Gamma,\mathbf d,F}$ for its coefficient algebra. For $\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, let $M_{\mathbf b,p}^{\epsilon}$ be a dressed minuscule class whose coweight has $b_i$ entries equal to $\epsilon$ at vertex $i$ and all other entries zero, where $0<\mathbf b\leq\mathbf d$. There is a finite expression $$\label{eq:root-charge-words}
 M_{\mathbf b,p}^{\epsilon}
   =\sum_r c_r a_{r1}\cdots a_{rk_r},
 \qquad c_r\in R_{\Gamma,\mathbf d,F},$$ in which every factor is topologically homogeneous and $$\deg_{\mathrm{top}}a_{rh}=\epsilon\boldsymbol\gamma_{rh},
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\gamma_{rh}\in\Delta_\Gamma,
 \qquad
 \sum_{h=1}^{k_r}\boldsymbol\gamma_{rh}=\mathbf b.$$ The factors need not themselves be minuscule classes.

If $\boldsymbol\gamma\in\Delta_\Gamma$ and $\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\boldsymbol\gamma=0$, then $$\mu_{\mathbb C}^{-1}(0)\cap
 \mu_{\mathbb R}^{-1}(\tau_{\boldsymbol\theta})\ne\varnothing.$$ The scalar circle acting simultaneously on all nonzero vertex spaces fixes every point of this representation.

u$-semistable point of $\mu^{-1}(0)$ is stable and has trivial $G$-stabilizer. Then the natural quotient map $$A_F/\langle (A_F)_m:m

u$-weight, is an isomorphism. This is an equality of quotients of $A_F$, preserving the coefficient map and both gradings.
